itinerary.cal: Usually snow-free from late spring through fall; the Haystack is best left alone when the slabs are wet or icy. A Discover Pass is needed at the trailhead, and this is always a single-day outing.
itinerary.totalNote: A one-day outing: hike the Mount Si Trail to Haystack Basin, scramble the Class 3 Haystack, and return the same way, about 8 miles and 3,500 ft round trip in 4-6 hours.

days.title: Hike Mount Si and scramble the Haystack
days.objective: Summit the Haystack and return to the trailhead
days.note: Steady, nearly continuous climb of about 4 miles to Haystack Basin (~3,900 ft), then a short, steep Class 3 scramble up the Haystack that gets slabby and exposed near the top. Downclimbing is slower than going up, so keep the party close and wear a helmet if others are above.

notes: WTA gives 8.0 mi RT and 3,150 ft to Haystack Basin (3,900 ft); the blog logs 8 mi, about 3,500 ft and 4h15m including the Haystack. The row's 3,360 ft and 6.8 km one-way (~8.5 mi RT) agree roughly; I used 3,500 ft (trailhead 668 ft to summit 4,167 ft per the row's waypoints). Hours is a typical-party figure; fast parties take about 4-4.5 h.

itinerary.cal: Best July through early October, after the South Fork Stillaguamish crossing drops and Headlee Pass melts out; earlier in the season expect snow from the pass up, which calls for an ice axe. Nearly every party does it as a single long day.
itinerary.totalNote: A one-day climb: Sunrise Mine Trail and the steep Headlee Pass switchbacks to Vesper Lake, then low-angle granite to the summit and back, about 8 miles and 4,000 ft in 7-9 hours.

days.title: Climb Vesper via Headlee Pass
days.objective: Summit Vesper Peak and return to the trailhead
days.note: Ford the unbridged creeks in the first mile (knee-deep in early summer), climb through forest and a talus basin, then the steep, crumbly short switchbacks up Headlee Pass, which most parties call the crux. Past Vesper Lake, follow a subtle rib up low-angle granite; skirt any lingering summit snowfield on the left.

schedule.label: Leave trailhead
schedule.detail: Water shoes help for the first creek crossings.

schedule.label: Top of Headlee Pass
schedule.detail: About 2.5 hours up, including some route-finding.

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: Snow from Vesper Lake to the base of the summit in early July.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: About 8 hours car to car, including roughly an hour lost off-route.

notes: WTA gives 8.0 mi RT and 4,000 ft, which matches the row's 4,000 ft; the row's 5.3 km one-way (6.6 mi RT) is a bit short of WTA's 8 mi. The schedule is from a single July 2024 WTA report (a solo hiker who lost about an hour). Steph Abegg's winter trip was 5h20 up and 3h20 down from the summer trailhead, plus an extra road walk.

itinerary.cal: Summer and fall are the usual season, though many parties prefer late winter or spring snow, which covers the brush and cliff bands below Price Lake. This is a day climb from the car; there are no established camps on this side.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day: Dingford Creek trail to Goat Creek, cross the valley, then pick through four cliff bands past Price Lake to the summit ridge, about 4,100 ft and 8-10 miles round trip.

days.title: Climb Price from the Dingford Creek trail
days.objective: Summit via the Price Lake basin and return
days.note: Leave the Dingford Creek trail at the Goat Creek crossing (~2,600 ft), find a log over Dingford Creek, and climb the Price Lake basin, staying east of its outlet creek. Expect brush and devil's club to about 4,000 ft, and cliff bands near 2,800, 3,200, 3,600 and 4,500 ft that need careful route-finding; the Price Creek gully between 3,200 and 3,800 ft is the most technical stretch.

notes: SummitPost gives 4-6 hours up, 4,100 ft and about 4 miles one-way (8 mi RT); The Mountaineers gives 10 mi RT and 4,100 ft. I used 9 mi as the midpoint. Total hours is an estimate (4-6 h up plus the descent). The row has no gain or distance figures.

itinerary.cal: Summer through fall. Snow ascents are possible but slow. It's the most direct line on the peak and a day trip from the car; a bike makes the road leg much quicker.
itinerary.totalNote: A one-day climb: walk or bike about 4 miles of the closed Middle Fork road to the Goldmyer spur, then climb about 3,700 ft of steep forest, talus and a Class 3 crest to the summit and return.

days.title: Road approach and climb the southeast spur
days.objective: Summit via the southeast spur ridge and return
days.note: From the Goldmyer Hot Springs spur (~1,800-1,900 ft), go straight up the forested north-south spur, angling left around a red cliff near 3,150 ft. Forest ends near 4,400-4,450 ft; cross the talus to the east-west crest near 5,100 ft, then follow its steep north side west to the summit, with some gendarmes and slippery duff.

notes: SummitPost gives 3,700 ft (matches the row), 3-5 hours and 2-3 miles one-way off the road, plus about 4 miles each way of road from the Dingford Creek trailhead. The 2001 Collins report took 3 hours of climbing when cars could still drive to Goldmyer. Miles is about 8 road plus about 5 off-trail round trip; hours is an estimate for walking the road (much less with a bike). The road leg adds little gain, which I didn't count separately.

reason: No source I could open describes the Noyes Basin line itself: only route-name lists (Wikipedia) and a Klenke report that climbed Seattle by the east basin from Low Divide. I couldn't confirm whether the row's Chicago Camp/Elwha approach is how parties do this route, so I didn't write a plan.

itinerary.cal: June through August has the best weather. An Olympic wilderness permit and a bear canister are required. It's a deep-interior peak, and most parties plan five days from the North Fork Quinault, usually combined with Christie, Noyes or Meany from the same Low Divide camp.
itinerary.totalNote: A five-day trip from the North Fork Quinault: two days hiking about 16 miles to Low Divide, a summit day up the Skyline Trail into upper Seattle Creek Basin and onto the Noyes-Seattle ridge, and two days out.

days.title: Hike the North Fork Quinault
days.objective: Reach Twelvemile camp
days.note: The first 12 miles of the North Fork Quinault trail are long but gentle, gaining only about 1,500 ft and losing about half of it again in ups and downs. Twelvemile camp is actually about 11.4 miles from the car.

days.title: Climb to the Low Divide camp
days.objective: Reach Low Divide (3,600 ft)
days.note: Cross to Sixteenmile camp (a ford, or a fallen log when one is in place), then gain most of the approach's elevation over the last 4 miles to Low Divide, the comfortable pass camp with a bear wire and a toilet.

days.title: Climb Seattle from Seattle Creek Basin
days.objective: Summit and return to Low Divide
days.note: Follow the Skyline Trail about 2 hours to the head of Seattle Creek Basin west of the peak, the site of the Seattle Meadows camp (~4,550 ft). Take the most direct line from the basin to the Noyes-Seattle ridge, then go around the rotten east side of the first summit to the slightly higher south peak.

days.title: Hike out to Halfway House
days.objective: Descend the North Fork Quinault
days.note: Retrace the trail down the valley; one party covered the 11 miles from Low Divide to Halfway House camp in about six hours.

days.title: Walk out to the trailhead
days.objective: Finish the last 5 miles
days.note: A short morning walk out to the North Fork Quinault trailhead.

notes: The Mazamas give 5,750 ft total gain for the Seattle Creek Basin route and 'two or more days'. Klenke's 2010 report supplies the approach splits (11.4 mi to Twelvemile; about 3,100 ft of up-and-down gain to Low Divide; Low Divide to the head of Seattle Creek Basin in about 2 h; 11 mi out to Halfway House in about 6 h). He actually climbed Seattle by the east basin (2.5 h up, 4.5 h round trip), so summit-day miles and hours here are estimates. Day gain/loss derived from Low Divide 3,600 ft and the summit 6,246 ft. Note that the Mazamas say the approach is about 19 mi, while the row's camp note and Klenke's mileage imply about 16.

reason: I found no openable source that mentions the Harniss Chute or describes a Mount Lincoln (Olympics) ascent with timing. Only Flapjack Lakes approach material and Sawtooth Ridge overviews turned up, so I didn't write a plan.

The sources I found cover the Northeast Ridge via Thornton Lakes; the only West Route mention is a SummitPost photo caption. There's no approach, camp or timing beta for the Triumph Pass approach, so I didn't write a plan.

itinerary.cal: Late July through September, once Spider Gap and the traverse snowfield are reasonable; bring an axe if the permanent snowfield near 7,000 ft is hard. Usually done as 3 days from Phelps Creek, often adding Cloudy Peak or Plummer Mountain.
itinerary.totalNote: A three-day trip: cross Spider Gap to Lyman Lakes and camp at Cloudy Pass, traverse around Cloudy Peak's south buttress to North Star the next day, and hike back over Spider Gap, about 31 miles round trip.

days.title: Over Spider Gap to Cloudy Pass
days.objective: Reach a camp at Cloudy Pass or Lyman Lakes
days.note: Hike Phelps Creek trail through Spider Meadow, climb about 800 ft of snow on the Spider Glacier to Spider Gap (~7,000 ft), drop into the Lyman Lakes basin, then follow the Cloudy Pass trail past Lyman Lake to camp at the pass. Watch for the reroute at Upper Lyman Lake's outlet.

days.title: Traverse around Cloudy Peak to North Star
days.objective: Summit North Star and return to Cloudy Pass
days.note: Leave the trail at the switchback toward Cloudy Peak's south ridge, round the buttress near 6,400 ft, and make a long traverse east (staying low to skip a talus field) to a permanent snowfield near 7,000 ft. Climb the main gully to the notch between the summits and scramble the southwest ridge. One party did the round trip from camp in an afternoon and evening.

days.title: Hike out over Spider Gap
days.objective: Return to the Phelps Creek trailhead
days.note: Descend to Lyman Lakes, climb back over Spider Gap, and descend Spider Meadow and the Phelps Creek trail to the car.

notes: The onehikeaweek report (Phelps Creek, 31.4 mi round trip, 3,520-8,096 ft) camped at Cloudy Pass and summited from there; Gimpilator's SummitPost log did Phelps Creek-Spider Gap-Cloudy Pass-North Star in day 1 of a 3-day loop. Per-day miles and gain are derived from the 31.4 mi total and elevations (trailhead 3,520, Spider Gap ~7,000, Lyman Lakes basin ~5,600, Cloudy Pass 6,440, summit 8,096), not quoted. WTA's 25 mi / 4,500 ft figure is for the Holden/Railroad Creek approach (the row's Holden Ballpark waypoint), which WTA lists as closed through summer 2026 due to storm damage.

itinerary.cal: Late July through September, when Spray Park is melted out; carry an ice axe and crampons or spikes for snow and the edge of the Flett Glacier. Normally one long day from Mowich Lake, often combined with Echo Rock.
itinerary.totalNote: A long single day from Mowich Lake: Spray Park Trail to the Echo-Observation saddle, around to the south slope, and up loose scree to the summit, about 12-13 miles and 3,500 ft in 10-12 hours.

days.title: Spray Park to Observation Rock
days.objective: Summit Observation Rock and return to Mowich Lake
days.note: Take the Spray Park Trail to the way trail near 6,200 ft and climb toward the Echo-Observation saddle near 7,600 ft. Contour around the foot of the peak (crossing the Flett Glacier's east icefield if present, watching for crevasses and moats) to the south-side scree, then climb loose volcanic rubble to the top. Many parties return via Knapsack Pass.

schedule.label: Leave Mowich Lake
schedule.detail: Approach via the Spray Park Trail.

schedule.label: Echo Rock (optional)
schedule.detail: This party tagged Echo Rock first and spent 30 minutes there.

schedule.label: Summit of Observation Rock
schedule.detail: Crampons for a steep snow section on the approach.

notes: WTA lists 'Observation Rock via Echo Rock' at 13.0 mi RT and 3,435 ft; one September 2024 party logged 12.7 mi in a little over 12 hours. The Mountaineers schedule (11 h car to car) includes Echo Rock, so Observation alone will be somewhat shorter. Both reports start at the Mowich Lake trailhead; the row says Mowich Lake is no longer drive-up, and that extra walk-in is NOT included in these figures.

itinerary.cal: July through October, when the PCT is snow-free; winter and spring ascents become snow scrambles with avalanche and icy-slope concerns. Always a single, half-day outing, easily combined with Tinkham or Abiel.
itinerary.totalNote: A half-day outing: PCT south from Windy Pass, a cairned side path to Abiel Pass, and a steep, rocky boot path to the summit, about 5.6 miles and 2,000 ft round trip.

days.title: PCT and Abiel Pass to Silver Peak
days.objective: Summit Silver Peak and return
days.note: Walk the PCT south about 1.7 miles to a cairned side trail that doubles back uphill (a tarn on your left means you overshot). Climb 0.3 mile with brief Class 2-3 moves to Abiel Pass (4,600 ft), then go right; the last 0.3 mile gains about 600 ft on loose rock.

notes: WTA gives 5.6 mi RT and 2,100 ft; The Mountaineers route page gives about 1,850 ft (8 mi on its loop variant). I used about 2,000 ft. Neither source gives a duration, so 4 h is an estimate, consistent with a Mountaineers report doing the comparable Tinkham loop from nearby in a little over 4 h.

itinerary.cal: June through October once snow is off the ridge; icy downsloping rock in shoulder season has turned parties back. Always a half-day trip, often made a loop over East Tinkham or combined with Silver and Abiel.
itinerary.totalNote: A half-day scramble: Mirror Lake trail and PCT to the Silver-Tinkham saddle, a boot path up the northwest ridge to the summit block, and usually a loop down via East Tinkham to Mirror Lake, 4-5 hours total.

days.title: Tinkham northwest ridge, loop via East Peak
days.objective: Summit Tinkham Peak and return to Mirror Lake trailhead
days.note: Hike the Mirror Lake trail and PCT to the turnoff for the Silver-Tinkham saddle (about 1.5 hours). Follow the boot path southeast up the northwest ridge, keeping right where the left side cliffs out, then climb steep, loose rock on the south side of the summit block. Wear helmets and stay out of each other's fall line.

schedule.label: Leave Mirror Lake trailhead
schedule.detail: Mirror Lake trail to the PCT, then north.

schedule.label: Silver-Tinkham saddle
schedule.detail: Helmets on before the ridge boot path.

schedule.label: Back at trailhead
schedule.detail: Little over 4 hours total, descending via East Tinkham and Mirror Lake.

notes: The Mountaineers route page gives 7.3 mi RT and 1,900 ft from Windy Pass; from the lower Mirror Lake trailhead (3,600 ft, per the row) to the 5,402 ft summit, I derived about 2,000 ft and about 6 mi for the loop. The schedule is from an August 2023 Mountaineers trip report. The summit time wasn't reported, so it's omitted.

itinerary.cal: June through October; this is the easiest way up either Tinkham summit and a short half day, often extended across the ridge to the main (west) summit.
itinerary.totalNote: A short half-day: Mirror Lake trail to the lake, then the boot path up the southeast spur to East Tinkham, about 4-5 miles and 1,800 ft round trip.

days.title: Mirror Lake and the East Tinkham boot path
days.objective: Summit East Tinkham and return
days.note: Hike about 1.2 miles to Mirror Lake, follow the PCT to the lake's south end, and take the worn boot path that leaves near 4,400 ft and climbs the southeast ridge to the east summit (5,395 ft). Easy scramble terrain continues west to the main summit if you want both.

notes: Gain is derived from the row's 3,600 ft trailhead to the 5,395 ft East Tinkham summit. Miles is approximate from the Mirror Lake distance (~1.2 mi each way per the Mountaineers/WTA Mirror Lake figures) plus the boot path. SummitPost log entries describe the SE route as an easy, well-worn boot path. No source times this route on its own, so hours is an estimate.

itinerary.cal: Late June through October once Commonwealth Basin melts out; earlier it's a snow climb with avalanche and icy-gully exposure. Most parties do Red Mountain as a single day; a Commonwealth Basin/Red Pond camp is optional, and an Alpine Lakes self-issue permit is required.
itinerary.totalNote: A one-day climb: PCT and the Commonwealth Basin trail to below the peak, a heather traverse to the red gully, and loose scrambling to the summit, about 7-8 miles and 2,900 ft in roughly 6 hours car to car.

days.title: Commonwealth Basin and the red gully
days.objective: Summit Red Mountain and return to Snoqualmie Pass
days.note: Follow the PCT north to the Commonwealth Basin trail and climb the basin about 2 miles until the peak comes into view, then traverse heather to the bright red gully/ramp. The rock is very loose, with frequent rockfall, so wear helmets and keep the party close. Descend the easier west-side scramble.

notes: The sources describe the standard Commonwealth Basin scramble and the SW face/ridge rather than this specific Class 4 'South Face' gully: 7.6 mi total via the Old Commonwealth Trail with a PCT return (Mountaineers 2025), and just under 6 h car to car (CascadeClimbers, winter SW face). Gain is derived from the roughly 3,000 ft trailhead to the 5,890 ft summit. SummitPost logs agree the rock is very loose.

itinerary.cal: July through early October, when the high trails are snow-free; a free self-issue wilderness permit is required. It can be done as a long day loop, but most parties camp a night at Sunny Pass or Horseshoe Basin to enjoy the tundra.
itinerary.totalNote: A two-day trip: hike the Boundary Trail to a camp at Sunny Pass or Horseshoe Basin, then climb Windy Peak by the Windy Peak Trail and loop back to Iron Gate via the Clutch Creek trail, about 15 miles and 3,800 ft in total.

days.title: Boundary Trail to Sunny Pass
days.objective: Camp at Sunny Pass or in Horseshoe Basin
days.note: Follow the Boundary Trail north through the 2006 Tripod Fire burn, crossing the Clutch Creek tributary at about 1.5 miles (the last reliable water before the basin), to Sunny Pass at about 4.8 miles. Horseshoe Basin's tundra camps are about 1.2 miles farther.

days.title: Climb Windy Peak and loop out
days.objective: Summit Windy Peak and return via Clutch Creek
days.note: From Sunny Pass take the Windy Peak Trail west, dropping to a saddle near 6,600 ft, staying left at the Basin Creek and Windy Creek junctions; a short spur gains the summit for 360-degree Pasayten views. Continue south on the Windy Peak Trail to the Clutch Creek trail and back to the Boundary Trail and trailhead.

notes: WTA's Windy Peak Loop from Iron Gate is 14.8 mi RT with 3,830 ft of gain; WTA Horseshoe Basin puts Sunny Pass at 4.8 mi (7,200 ft). Gilbert's report confirms the route from Sunny Pass via the 6,600 ft saddle. Per-day splits are derived (day 1 about 1,300 ft per the Horseshoe Basin figures; day 2 is the rest of the loop). The row's 9.66 km one-way (6 mi) matches the distance to Horseshoe Basin rather than to the summit; an out-and-back via Sunny Pass is longer than the loop. WTA lists the summit at 8,060-8,100 ft against the row's 8,335.

itinerary.cal: July through September; the Liberty Bell-Concord gully holds snow (sometimes icy) into late June, and rockfall picks up once it melts. A short one-day climb, often linked with Liberty Bell or Lexington Tower.
itinerary.totalNote: A one-day climb: Blue Lake Trail and climbers' path to the Liberty Bell-Concord notch, a short multi-pitch line to the summit, rappels down the North Face, and out the same way, about 6-7 hours car to car.

days.title: Approach the notch and climb Concord Tower
days.objective: Summit Concord Tower and return to the trailhead
days.note: Hike the Blue Lake Trail about 1.5 miles, take the climbers' path past a small stream up slabs, talus and heather into the Liberty Bell-Concord gully, and from the notch drop about 50 ft on the north side to the Cave Route start. The climbing takes under two hours; descend with four rappels down the North Face (a 60 m rope is required) back to the notch.

notes: No source describes this variation itself. The plan uses the shared Cave Route start and descent: SummitPost gives 'less than two hours' of climbing and the 4-rappel North Face descent; Steph Abegg gives about 1 h from the notch to the Blue Lake Trail plus 30-45 min out, and just over an hour to climb the neighboring North Face. Gain is derived from the 5,200 ft trailhead to the row's 7,569 ft high point. Miles and total hours are estimates.

reason: The only beta I found names the Tower Route in passing (approach from the Ice Caves trail, and a CascadeClimbers note about Tower 1's lower pitches). I found no source giving the full route length, timing, or whether parties go car-to-car, so I didn't write a plan.

The trip reports I found climb Big Snow via Myrtle Lake and Big Snow/Snowflake lakes (17 mi, 5,500 ft, 14.5 h car to car, SummitPost 2013); one report only mentions seeing a line on the southwest side above Hester Lake. With no source for the Hester Lake/SW ridge line, I didn't write a plan.

itinerary.cal: Mid-July through September, once the Chain Lakes trail and Bullseye Pass are snow-free; bring a 40 m rope, harnesses and helmets for the roped section. Usually done as the 3-day Bullseye Traverse from Stevens Pass to the Whitepine trailhead (a car shuttle is needed).
itinerary.totalNote: A three-day Bullseye Traverse: Stevens Pass to camp at Chain Lakes, drop packs at Bullseye Pass for a 4.5-hour side trip up Bull's Tooth's south side and continue to camp near Frosty Pass, then hike out to Whitepine.

days.title: Stevens Pass to Chain Lakes
days.objective: Camp at Middle Chain Lake
days.note: Follow the PCT past Lake Susan Jane and Josephine Lake, descend the Icicle Creek trail to the Chain Lakes junction, then grind up about 2,100 ft in 2.5 miles on the Chain Lakes trail to the lakes. Middle Chain Lake has secluded sites with views of the Upper Icicle peaks.

days.title: Bull's Tooth from Bullseye Pass
days.objective: Summit Bull's Tooth and move camp toward Frosty Pass
days.note: Climb to Bullseye Pass, drop packs below the peak, and scramble the steep southeast slope and a Class 3 traverse to beneath the summit. About one long pitch of Class 4-5 on the south ridge (40 m rope) reaches the top; three rappels from slung rocks return to the scramble terrain. Then continue past the Doelle Lakes to camp just below Frosty Pass.

schedule.label: Bullseye Pass
schedule.detail: About 30 minutes from camp; drop packs below the Tooth.

schedule.label: Back at packs
schedule.detail: The summit side trip took about 4.5 hours round trip including three rappels.

days.title: Frosty Pass to Whitepine
days.objective: Hike out to the Whitepine trailhead
days.note: Cross Frosty Pass and descend, with an optional steep side trip of about 1,150 ft to Lake Grace, then descend to the Whitepine trailhead for the pickup.

notes: Day distance, gain and hours are converted from Brooke Beyond's stats: 17 km/1,070 m/7 h; 10 km/540 m/3.5 h plus a 4.5 h summit side trip; 23 km/700 m/7 h (day 3 includes the Lake Grace side trip). Her description (south ridge, 40 m rope, three rappels) matches the row. Climber Kyle confirms the Stevens Pass-PCT-Chain Lakes overnight approach, but he climbed a third-class line from above the upper lake. Loss figures are rough derivations, not quoted. Note that the three blog URLs are one author's single trip, so these figures come from essentially one party.

reason: I found no openable trip report or route page for the North Ridge; only Wikipedia-mirror first-ascent notes and a Yellowleaf index that I couldn't confirm covers this route. The ford and approach detail in the row couldn't be corroborated, so I didn't write a plan.

The sources cover the C-J col approach for Johannesburg routes (bivy at the col, meadow camp near 6,200 ft); none mentions the Northwest Chimney on Cascade Peak or gives its timing, so I didn't write a plan.

The row has no data. The east-side reports I found (Collins 2006, linked from SummitPost; Stevensong 2023) approach from Manning Park in Canada, which isn't a lawful border crossing. The documented lawful US approach (Ross Lake boat, Lightning and Freezeout creeks; Lemke 2023, 39 mi walking, 27.5 h push) climbs the west slopes, not the East Ridge.
The row has no data, and no source I found describes a North Ridge route or itinerary on Castle Peak (Pasayten).

Only first-ascent material exists, and that party approached from Canada (not lawful). I found no source giving an itinerary, camps or timing for the lawful Ross Lake/Freezeout Creek approach to the north face, so I didn't write a plan.

itinerary.cal: July through September; early season brings snow on the Barrier and in the basin. Plan at least three days from Goodell Creek with a settled forecast, and get a North Cascades National Park cross-country permit.
itinerary.totalNote: A three-day Southern Pickets trip: Goodell Creek and the Barrier to a Crescent Creek Basin camp, a long day across the basin to the Himmelhorn-West Twin Needle notch and up the Class 4 original route, then about 5 hours back out.

days.title: Goodell Creek and the Barrier to the basin
days.objective: Camp in Crescent Creek Basin
days.note: Walk about 4 miles of old roadbed to the cairn near 1,800 ft, continue north to the Terror Creek crossing (~2,100 ft), then climb the steep Barrier boot path up the forested ridge to timberline at Stump Hollow (~5,600-6,000 ft). Traverse to the ~6,400 ft saddle northeast of the Chopping Block and drop into Crescent Creek Basin. Stump Hollow is the fallback camp if the day runs long.

days.title: Climb West Twin Needle from the notch
days.objective: Summit West Twin Needle and return to basin camp
days.note: Traverse the basin west to the notch between the Himmelhorn and West Twin Needle, then climb the original route, mostly Class 3-4 with a short harder section near the top. Descend the Class 2 west slope to the notch; expect downclimbing and possibly rappels on any gully descent.

days.title: Hike out to Goodell Creek
days.objective: Return to the Goodell Creek trailhead
days.note: Reclimb to the Chopping Block saddle and descend the Barrier and the roadbed; the Crescent Creek side is brushier and harder to follow on the way down than the Terror Basin path.

notes: Abegg's 2009 Twin Needles trip (Thread of Ice, a different line) was 3 days: approach to Crescent Creek Basin, a climb day ending on West Twin Needle (Class 3-4, ~5.6 crux below the west summit), and about 5 h back to the car. Her Pickets page supplies the approach elevations (cairn ~1,800, Terror Creek ~2,100, Stump Hollow ~5,600, saddle ~6,400). The AAC note only says the West Needle is easy from the notch area; I found no description of this route's 'West Slope - East Arete' line beyond that. Day gain is derived from the row's waypoints (500 ft roadhead, 6,050 ft basin camp, 7,936 ft summit). Miles and summit-day hours are estimates.
